lore_anchors.definition: A rare creature listed in the Strange Insect Register, ranked around number 100; known for its beautiful, crystalline white body and significant spiritual potential.
A competitive ranking of rare spirit beasts and insects in the cultivation world, serving as a quick gauge of a creature's value and threat level.
A warning bell system used by major sects; a count of eighty-one tolls signals an imminent sect-wide annihilation.
A cultivator's most vital life force; using it for a soul-control restriction creates a permanent, irreversible bond between master and spirit beast.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li destroy the original storage pouch?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He suspects it may carry a tracking mark or identity-inscribing spell that a higher-level cultivator planted on it; in the Mortal Stream, destroying enemy gear is standard paranoid security.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the bell ringing eighty-one times?
cultural_notes_faq.a: In sect lore and Daoist numerology, eighty-one is the product of nine times nine, the highest yang number, and is reserved exclusively for signaling a sect-destroying calamity—an irreversible loss.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li distrust the Imperial Spirit Sect cultivator's confession?
cultural_notes_faq.a: A dying confession is a tactical transaction, not a truth-telling. Han Li's doubt is the natural reflex of a Mortal Stream survivor: he treats every piece of intelligence as a potential trap until independently confirmed.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why do the white spider hatchlings imprint on Han Li as 'parent'?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The soul-control restriction used the cultivator's Essence Blood, which carries a fragment of their fundamental life essence. The spiders bond to the blood's source, not to the concept of a 'master,' creating an irreversible, instinct-driven loyalty.
